people.name: Daniel A. Low
people.title: Professor and Vice Chair of Medical Physics Research and Innovation, Department of Radiation Oncology, UCLA
people.bio: Developed the breathing motion model behind 5DCT in 2005 and has led its development and clinical implementation at UCLA. A.B. in Physics, Occidental College; Ph.D. in Physics, Indiana University. Recipient of the 2026 ASTRO Gold Medal.

people.name: Drew Moghanaki
people.title: Professor and Chief of Thoracic Oncology, Department of Radiation Oncology, UCLA. Stanley Iezman and Nancy Stark Endowed Chair in Thoracic Radiation Oncology Research
people.bio: Thoracic radiation oncologist and clinical partner for 5DCT in lung cancer treatment planning. Leads national lung cancer research including the VALOR trial of stereotactic radiotherapy versus surgery. M.D., Vanderbilt University; residency, University of Pennsylvania. ASTRO Fellow, 2025.

people.name: Michael V. Lauria
people.title: Assistant Professor, Department of Radiation Oncology, UCLA
people.role: Faculty; clinical workflow and motion-compensated CBCT
people.bio: Completed his Ph.D. in the lab in 2022 on applications of breathing motion dynamics from fast-helical free-breathing CT, then the UCLA medical physics residency, and joined the faculty in 2024. Led the retrospective analysis of the first clinical 5DCT workflow and the motion-compensated cone-beam CT pilot study.

people.name: Claudia R. Miller
people.title: Resident, Department of Radiation Oncology, UCLA
people.bio: Ph.D. in Physics and Biology in Medicine, 2026. Her dissertation improved the clinical 5DCT workflow with diaphragm-based calibration of the breathing signal and a 4DCT HiFi backup, then measured how 4DCT- and 5DCT-defined target volumes differ in blinded physician contouring and in the resulting dose distributions.

people.name: Ryan Andosca
people.title: Ph.D. candidate, Physics and Biology in Medicine, UCLA
people.bio: Advanced to candidacy in 2026. Works on correcting 5DCT images for ventilation-induced density change, density-based regional ventilation mapping, motion-compensated cone-beam CT for tracking tumor response during treatment, and the stability of patient-specific motion models over a course of radiotherapy.
